class.name: TressFXCollisionMesh
class.brief_description: A mesh that [TressFXHair] strands are kept out of.
class.description: Turns a mesh into a signed distance field on the GPU and rebuilds it whenever the mesh moves. The source is either a [code].tfxmesh[/code] file exported from Maya or Blender (the Blender to Godot Hair add-on) or any Godot [Mesh] (a [SphereMesh] or [CapsuleMesh] primitive, or a skinned mesh whose bone weights follow [member hair_skeleton]). Add the node to a hair's [member TressFXHair.collision_meshes] and the hair stays outside it. Closed, evenly tessellated meshes work best: the distance field is only built in a narrow band around the surface, and open edges make hair kink along them. A body proxy of a few thousand triangles is plenty. A hair groom's rest pose must lie outside its colliders; see [member TressFXHair.collision_skip_root_vertices] for grooms rooted inside the skin. In the editor the collider is drawn as an orange shape in the pose the distance field uses. Unselected, only the parts outside the body show; selecting the collider, or a [TressFXHair] that lists it, draws the whole shape on top. The [b]Hair Colliders[/b] button in the 3D editor's toolbar (Editor Setting [code]tressfx/editor/show_collision_shapes[/code]) hides and shows them. In the editor a [code].tfxmesh[/code] written again by an exporter is reloaded within a second or two.

method.name: debug_print_distances
method.description: Debug helper: reads the whole distance field back from the GPU and prints the signed distance at the given world-space points.

method.name: get_cell_count
method.description: Cells per axis of the distance field grid, padding included.

method.name: get_cpu_time_usec
method.description: Main-thread time spent by this node in the last frame, in microseconds.

method.name: get_triangle_count
method.description: Number of triangles in the loaded mesh.

method.name: get_vertex_count
method.description: Number of vertices in the loaded mesh.

members.member: Hair is kept this many cells away from the surface. Keep it at 0 for hair rooted on the mesh; a hand pushing through fur can use 0.5.
Bone whose motion moves the distance field grid with the mesh (the root bone for a body, a forearm for a hand). Without one the grid follows this node.
Skeleton driving the mesh. The bone names in a [code].tfxmesh[/code], or the bone weights of a skinned [member mesh], must belong to it. Changing it reloads the mesh.
Multiplies vertex positions on load; use 0.01 for an asset authored in centimetres. Changing it reloads the mesh.
Alternative to [member tfxmesh_path]: any mesh, first surface only. Bone weights are used when present. Changing it reloads the mesh.

Cells across the mesh's bounding cube; the grid is padded by 80% on every side, so the total is about 2.6 times this per axis. Finer grids cut resting jitter (50 to 80 cut it threefold on the AMD sample) at the cost of GPU memory and build time. Changing it reloads the mesh.
Most a hair vertex is pushed out per frame, in cells. Deep vertices emerge over a few frames instead of teleporting to the surface and flickering back; 0.25 is a good value for a body.
A [code].tfxmesh[/code] collision mesh exported by the TressFX Maya exporter (bone names, skinned vertices and triangles). Changing it reloads the mesh.
